excluded_points.reason: outside boundary — config-server owns and can remediate its own availability; api-gateway has no authority over it

points.target: client-facing entry surface (ApiGatewayController /api/gateway/** + Spring Cloud Gateway proxy routes /api/vet/**, /api/visit/**, /api/customer/**, /api/genai/**)

set_aside.name: gateway-level Retry filter (retries=1, statuses=SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, methods=POST) applied to proxy routes
set_aside.evidence: application.yml:14-18 — this is an SE/CE-class outbound protection on the proxy path, not an EE inbound protection (rate limiting/bulkhead); logged here because it is adjacent evidence, not scored under EE

mechanisms.name: circuit_breaker
mechanisms.resolution_path: no ReactiveCircuitBreaker, no Resilience4j annotation, no gateway CircuitBreaker filter wraps this specific WebClient call (the gateway-level CircuitBreaker filter in application.yml applies only to Spring Cloud Gateway proxy routes, not to this internally-issued WebClient call)

mechanisms.name: retry
mechanisms.resolution_path: no .retry() / .retryWhen() operator on the Mono chain

mechanisms.name: timeout
mechanisms.resolution_path: no .responseTimeout() / .timeout() operator, no HttpClient customization, no application.yml spring.cloud.gateway.httpclient.response-timeout or reactor.netty client config found; WebClient.Builder used with no customization at injection point (checked: no @Bean WebClient.Builder customizer found in ApiGatewayApplication.java or elsewhere)
mechanisms.evidence: CustomersServiceClient.java:23-25 (constructor, unmodified builder); grep across module: no timeout config found

mechanisms.name: connection_pool
mechanisms.resolution_path: Reactor Netty default connection pool applies implicitly; no explicit ConnectionProvider bean or pool-size config found in repo

mechanisms.name: circuit_breaker
mechanisms.resolution_path: code-level instantiation, no explicit resilience4j.circuitbreaker.instances.getOwnerDetails config block found anywhere in repo (defaults apply, exact threshold/window UNVERIFIED in-repo)
mechanisms.condition_applied: prerequisite 'timeout' UNVERIFIED (no explicit TimeLimiter/timeout config found for this breaker in-repo) -> conditional else-branch applied (1 instead of 3)

mechanisms.name: fallback
mechanisms.resolution_path: code-level, does not call any other dependency (not circular)
mechanisms.condition_applied: prerequisite 'timeout or circuit_breaker' satisfied (circuit_breaker present) -> full weight

mechanisms.name: timeout
mechanisms.resolution_path: same as CE-1 — no explicit timeout config found in-repo for this call path

mechanisms.name: readiness_probe
mechanisms.resolution_path: spring-boot-starter-actuator IS a declared dependency (pom.xml) so /actuator/health exists in the running app, but docker-compose.yml defines NO healthcheck stanza for the api-gateway service (contrast with config-server and discovery-server, which do have one), and no Kubernetes manifests exist in this repository. The mechanism exists in the dependency tree but is not verifiably wired to any container-level probe in this repo.
mechanisms.evidence: pom.xml (actuator dep present); docker-compose.yml:71-82 (no healthcheck key, compare to lines for config-server/discovery-server which have one)

mechanisms.name: graceful_shutdown
mechanisms.resolution_path: no server.shutdown: graceful found in any application.yml in this module

mechanisms.name: declared_resource_limits
mechanisms.resolved_value: PARTIAL — memory limit 512M only, no CPU limit, no reservation/request of any kind
mechanisms.note: profile requires CPU+memory request AND limit for credit; only memory limit present, so this does not meet the bar for the weight-2 item

mechanisms.name: disruption_policy
mechanisms.resolution_path: no Kubernetes manifests in repository; concept does not apply to docker-compose

totals.domains_rationale: api-gateway serves a single functional domain: read-aggregation of owner/pet/visit data for the client. All endpoints and proxy routes serve that one purpose; no unrelated business capability is co-located.

remediation.action: Add an explicit response timeout to the customers-service WebClient call (CE-1)
remediation.rationale: Closes the single largest exposure: this call currently has zero time bound and can hang indefinitely.

remediation.action: Wrap the customers-service call in a circuit breaker (CE-1), with the timeout above as prerequisite for full credit
remediation.rationale: Limits blast radius once the timeout exists; without the timeout the breaker cannot trip on hangs.

remediation.action: Add a fallback for the customers-service call (CE-1)
remediation.rationale: The visits-service path already degrades gracefully to an empty list; the customers-service path has no equivalent and currently fails the whole request.

remediation.action: Wire /actuator/health into a container-level readiness and liveness probe (docker-compose healthcheck, or Kubernetes probes if deployed there)
remediation.rationale: The health-check machinery already exists via Actuator; it is simply not connected to anything that acts on it.

remediation.action: Configure a specific liveness probe distinct from readiness, then enable self-healing (restart policy tied to liveness failure)
remediation.rationale: Enables automatic recovery once the probe exists.

remediation.action: Enable graceful shutdown (server.shutdown: graceful) with a bounded grace period
remediation.rationale: Prevents in-flight request loss on every redeploy — currently every deployment is a small outage for requests in flight.

remediation.action: Declare CPU limit and both CPU+memory reservations, not memory limit alone
remediation.rationale: Closes the resource-limits item; low individual weight but easy to ship alongside the above.

remediation.action: Add a rate limiter or bulkhead at the gateway's own entry surface (EE-1)
remediation.rationale: Nothing currently bounds concurrent/rate load on the gateway's own endpoint before it fans out to two downstream calls.

remediation.action: Confirm (and if absent, configure) an explicit timeout and connection pool for the visits-service call (CE-2), and confirm the circuit breaker's own timeout so it earns full conditional credit
remediation.rationale: CE-2 is currently the strongest path but still rests on unverified framework defaults rather than explicit configuration.
